test.title: Trees that keep their dead leaves

paragraphs.text: Most deciduous trees drop their leaves in autumn, but some, including young beech and oak trees, keep many dead brown leaves on their branches until spring. This habit has puzzled botanists for over a century, and several explanations have been proposed.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: One idea is that the dead leaves protect buds from animals. Deer prefer not to eat dry, papery leaves, so a branch covered in them may be left alone. Supporters point out that the habit is most common on young trees and on the lower branches of older ones, which are within reach of deer.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: A second explanation concerns nutrients. If leaves fall in spring rather than autumn, they decay around the tree just as it begins to grow, providing food at the moment it is most needed.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Neither idea has been proved. A field study in Denmark found that deer did eat fewer buds on beech trees that kept their leaves, but the difference was small. Some researchers now suspect that the habit has no single purpose and may simply be left over from the evolutionary history of these trees.
paragraphs.label: D

document.title: Trees that keep their dead leaves

items.quote: some, including young beech and oak trees, keep many dead brown leaves on their branches until spring
items.prompt: Trees that keep dead leaves until spring

options.text: are common among all deciduous trees.
include young beech and oak trees.
lose all their leaves in autumn.
are found mainly in Denmark.

explanation.en: “some, including young beech and oak trees, keep many dead brown leaves” → B. “Most deciduous trees drop their leaves”, so it is not all trees (A). Denmark (D) is only where one study took place.
explanation.kk: «some, including young beech and oak trees, keep many dead brown leaves» → B. «Most deciduous trees drop their leaves» — демек бұл барлық ағашқа тән емес (A). Дания (D) — бір зерттеудің орны ғана.
explanation.ru: «some, including young beech and oak trees, keep many dead brown leaves» → B. «Most deciduous trees drop their leaves» — значит, это не все деревья (A). Дания (D) — только место одного исследования.

items.quote: the dead leaves protect buds from animals
items.prompt: According to the first explanation, dead leaves may

options.text: keep the tree warm in winter.
attract useful insects.
store water for the tree.
stop deer from eating the buds.

explanation.en: “the dead leaves protect buds from animals. Deer prefer not to eat dry, papery leaves” → D. Warmth, insects and water (A–C) are not mentioned.
explanation.kk: «the dead leaves protect buds from animals. Deer prefer not to eat dry, papery leaves» → D. Жылу, жәндік және су (A–C) мәтінде аталмайды.
explanation.ru: «the dead leaves protect buds from animals. Deer prefer not to eat dry, papery leaves» → D. Тепло, насекомые и вода (A–C) в тексте не упоминаются.

items.quote: on the lower branches of older ones, which are within reach of deer
items.prompt: Supporters of the first explanation point out that the habit is most common

options.text: on the highest branches.
on branches that deer can reach.
on trees growing in open fields.
in dry climates.

explanation.en: “on young trees and on the lower branches of older ones, which are within reach of deer” → B. A is the opposite of “lower branches”.
explanation.kk: «on young trees and on the lower branches of older ones, which are within reach of deer» → B. A — «lower branches» дегенге қарама-қарсы.
explanation.ru: «on young trees and on the lower branches of older ones, which are within reach of deer» → B. A — противоположность «lower branches».

items.quote: they decay around the tree just as it begins to grow, providing food at the moment it is most needed
items.prompt: The second explanation suggests that leaves falling in spring

options.text: provide nutrients when the tree starts growing.
protect the roots from frost.
prevent other plants from growing.
are eaten by deer.

explanation.en: “they decay around the tree just as it begins to grow, providing food” → A: “nutrients” = “food”. The other options are not in the text.
explanation.kk: «they decay around the tree just as it begins to grow, providing food» → A: «nutrients» = «food». Қалған нұсқалар мәтінде кездеспейді.
explanation.ru: «they decay around the tree just as it begins to grow, providing food» → A: «nutrients» = «food». Остальные варианты в тексте не встречаются.

items.quote: deer did eat fewer buds on beech trees that kept their leaves, but the difference was small
items.prompt: What did the field study in Denmark find?

options.text: Deer avoided beech trees completely.
The leaves made only a small difference to how many buds deer ate.
The leaves had no effect at all on deer.
Oak trees kept more leaves than beech trees.

explanation.en: “deer did eat fewer buds … but the difference was small” → B. A exaggerates (“completely”), and C denies an effect that did exist.
explanation.kk: «deer did eat fewer buds … but the difference was small» → B. A асыра айтады («completely»), C бар әсерді жоққа шығарады.
explanation.ru: «deer did eat fewer buds … but the difference was small» → B. A преувеличивает («completely»), C отрицает эффект, который всё же был.

groups.instruction: Questions 1–5. Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.
